name: Question 1
problem:
Consider the following relation defined on the set $A={1,3,5,7}.$ 

$$
R={(1,3),(1,5),(3,5),(5,7)}
$$

Select the options that make the following reasoning correct:

We have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(1,1){{field-1}}R,\,(3,3){{field-2}}R,\,(5,5){{field-3}}R,\,(7,7){{field-4}}R\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since 
{{field-5}}{{field-6}}, 

the relation is 
{{field-7}}.
worked_solution:
A binary relation $R,$ defined on a set $A,$ is 

- *reflexive* if $(x,x)\in R$ for all $x\in A,$

- *irreflexive* if $(x,x)\notin R$ for all $x\in A.$

If some pairs of the form $(x,x)$ belong to a relation and others do not, then the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.

In our case, the relation is defined on ${1,3,5,7},$ and we have

$$
(1,1)\notin R,\,(3,3)\notin R,\,(5,5)\notin R,\,(7,7)\notin R.
$$

Therefore, we can conclude the following:

$\,$ Since $(x,x)\notin R$ $\text{for all }x\in A,$ the relation is $\text{irreflexive}.$

EXPLANATION

A binary relation R, defined on a set A, is

  • reflexive if (x,x)∈R for all x∈A,

  • irreflexive if (x,x)∉R for all x∈A.

If some pairs of the form (x,x) belong to a relation and others do not, then the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.

In our case, the relation is defined on {1,3,5,7}, and we have

(1,1)∉R,(3,3)∉R,(5,5)∉R,(7,7)∉R.

Therefore, we can conclude the following:

Since (x,x)∉R for all x∈A, the relation is irreflexive.
